newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends lower on weak earnings.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends lower on weak earnings.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly lower on Tuesday, pulled down by a series of poor company results in the last days of the corporate reporting season, analysts said.
The foreign currency B index shed 0.64 points or 0.36 percent to 175.89 on turnover of HK$148.3 million compared with Monday's HK$273.8 million.
"Companies with unattractive results usually wait until the end of the season to publish their reports, and investors are cautious over these few days," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
April 30 is the deadline for issuing 1996 annual results.
The holiday mood already taking over was reducing trading volume, brokers said.
The Shenzhen and Shanghai stock exchanges will be closed on May 1 and 2 for the Labour Day holiday.
"The index is not going to move drastically in a three-day week," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said, adding the index has found support at the 175 point level.
Selling of firms with weak earnings set the tone for Tuesday's trading, brokers said.
SEZ Real Estate dived to its 10 percent daily limit-down in early morning trading for the second straight session after announcing poor 1996 annual results over the weekend.
It recovered much of the loss by the close but was still the worst performer with a fall of HK$0.17 or 4.18 percent to HK$3.90.
The company posted a net loss of 26.34 million yuan for 1996 based on international accounting standards.
"People did not expect such bad results from SEZ," an analyst at J&A Securities said. "But selling has slowed after the sharp declines."
Shenzhen North Jianshe Motorcycle was the top gainer despite announcing sharply lower profits for 1996. It closed at its 10 percent limit-up of HK$3.81 on volume of 827,100 shares.
"Although the results were terrible, they beat expectations as the motor industry had gone through a rough year," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
Jianshe said net profits for 1996 plunged to 50.73 million yuan from 288.71 million in 1995 based on international accounting standards.
Losses in the domestic currency A share market also contributed to the B share dips, traders said.
The A share index lost 3.52 points or 0.72 percent to 484.72 on a correction, analysts said. Turnover reached 14.9 billion yuan.
